owner: Claude Design (UI contract). Tessera receipts are the source of truth; Antigravity serves them; Claude Code builds the page.
answers: FOR-CLAUDE-DESIGN.md ask 1 (event contract), ask 2 (the 'added to the library' moment) and ask 3 (honest empty and slow states).
principle: The page animates only from these events. One event per receipt. Nothing loops, nothing pretends to progress, and a page never keeps its own copy of a request (MUST-FOLLOW 12: surfaces render nouns from Tessera).

transport.stream: GET /api/requests/:id/events?after=<seq> (Server-Sent Events, optional). Without it, poll the snapshot.
transport.pause_rule: After 3 failed polls show 'Live updates paused · Try again' and freeze all motion.
transport.public_vs_private: One public page per request (/requests/:id), in the third person. The nonprofit unlocks the 'you' wording and the decision buttons by typing its request code into the page (sent once as Authorization: Bearer, kept only in memory). No credential ever goes in a URL. See claude-design-signin-and-console.v1.json -> request_code.

at.description: UTC time from the Tessera receipt.

request_id.description: The one id of the request noun. Used in the URL. Never a second display alias.

harness.description: As declared by the worker. Shown as declared, never verified by the page.

kind.description: Who runs the worker. 'volunteer' = anyone's agent on a volunteer key, using their spare capacity. 'eranos_worker' = one of the 1-3 dedicated workers the ta-amps team runs so no request waits forever. Both claim, do and report through Tessera like any worker; neither is a second queue.

run_by.description: For eranos_worker: 'ta-amps team'. Shown in the technical layer.

allowance.description: For eranos_worker (MUST-FOLLOW 8, server inference): {payer, provider, model, budget_usd_remaining, deadline}. Shown in the technical layer; every attempt keeps its receipt.

data.title: short plain title (<= 60 chars)
data.example_request: boolean; true only for made-up example requests showing how the request page works

data.fallback_at: date-time or null: when one of Eranos's own workers will claim it if no volunteer has. Volunteers get the first chance. Null when no dedicated worker is running.

part.claimed.ui: Label the helper by actor.kind: 'A volunteer's AI' or 'One of Eranos's own workers'.

part.heartbeat.ui: one ping on the helper ring; no text

review.claimed.ui: Same labels. The checker must be a different worker and key from the maker, whatever its kind: with one dedicated worker it can make or check, never both.

review.refused.ui: The refusal card exists only when this event exists.

data.eranos_library_url: /catalog/<id> (the Eranos 'Library' nav item keeps the existing /catalog routes)

plain_copy.rule: Two voices. 'you' only when the page holds the request code (the tab that sent the request, or after the code is typed into band 4); 'the nonprofit' or the organization label otherwise. No worker ids, request ids, hashes or HTTP codes in the plain view.

estimates.rule: Show 'usually picked up in A–B min' only when the queue had at least 10 claims in the last 7 days and one in the last 24 h. A and B are the 25th and 75th percentile of the last 50 claim delays. Otherwise show no estimate.
estimates.no_volunteers_online: When volunteers_online is 0 and fallback_at is set, show the fallback time ('If none is free by 2:30 PM, one of Eranos's own workers will pick it up'). When fallback_at is null too, say plainly that nobody is online, keep the place in line, and offer 'Share the I want to help page' and 'See a finished request like this'. Never animate a helper that is not there.

motion.send_to_page: Cross-document View Transition from the form (view-transition-name: request) to the page header, 480 ms, cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1). Fallback: plain navigation.
motion.request.split: Part cards enter left to right, 60 ms stagger, opacity 0->1 and 4 px rise, 200 ms.
motion.part.claimed: The helper chip slides onto the part (320 ms); one orange dot carries the part title along the edge to the helper at 200 CSS px/s.
motion.part.heartbeat: One ring ping (opacity 0.4->0, scale 1->1.6, 600 ms). Never more than one per heartbeat.
motion.part.object_made: The checklist row turns from 'Not yet' to 'Made' (120 ms crossfade).
motion.review.refused: The refusal card enters with a 2 px rust outline; no shake, no red flash.
motion.review.verdict: Approved: the check card turns green with a check (200 ms). Sent back: amber with a return arrow.
motion.library.added: The deliverable chips travel to the 'Shared library' box (one at a time, 600 ms each), then the box shows the count.
motion.reduced_motion: No dots, slides or pings. State changes are 120 ms crossfades. The View Transition is skipped.
motion.aria_live: polite: one sentence per event, the plain_copy line.

replay.what: Plays the recorded events in order on the same page. It is a replay of things that happened, labeled 'Replay' in the page's own controls.
replay.start: Button 'Replay' (finished requests and examples only) or ?replay=1 for capture.
replay.hold_s: for each event: max(2.0, 0.5 + words/3.0) of its plain_copy line; band changes add the scroll time
replay.scroll: Auto-scroll to the band that changes, <= 800 CSS px/s, then hold 2 s. A user scroll stops auto-scroll for the rest of the replay.
replay.controls: Replay · Stop · step dots (1-4). Escape stops.
replay.never: Faster than reading speed. The live page never uses the 1.35 s timer of the current build.

from_current_snapshot.note: Until the events endpoint exists, the page derives events from the current GET /api/requests/:id payload (COORDINATION_CONTRACT.md section 2A). Times come from receipts when present; otherwise the events carry no time and the timeline shows no clock.

dedicated_workers.owner_direction: Nov 1: 1-3 dedicated server workers pick up tasks even when no volunteer worker is available; this also lets the film record real pickups.
rules: They are ordinary authorized workers on Tessera: claim, do, report, leases, receipts. No second queue, no hidden server agent.
Volunteers get the first chance: a dedicated worker claims only after fallback_at (set per queue by the operator).
Every dedicated-worker attempt records purpose, payer (ta-amps team), provider and model, allowance and deadline (MUST-FOLLOW 8).
Maker and checker are always different workers and keys. With a single dedicated worker, a check waits for a volunteer or a second worker.
The page never calls a dedicated worker 'a volunteer'. The film's 'a volunteer's AI' lines are gated on the claim's worker kind.
dedicated_workers.estimates: With dedicated workers running, the waiting state shows the fallback time instead of 'no volunteer online'.
